findings.title: Default work completion accepts any existing file as 'tests' evidence, and no surveyed repository enables verified completion
findings.boundary: Praxis work-completion gate (plain `work complete`) in the default policy used by every surveyed repository
findings.statement: With the default scaffold ros.json, `praxis work complete --evidence implementation=README.md --evidence tests=/etc/hostname --conclusion 'all tests pass'` moves the item to complete. The check only confirms that the evidence types are present and the paths exist. Nothing runs, parses or binds the evidence to a revision, and the path may be outside the repository. `praxis verify` exits 0 and `work validate` reports valid with 0 findings afterwards. None of the 45 ros.json files surveyed (16 local repositories, 29 ext clones) sets requireVerifiedCompletion, requireAttestedEvidence or trustedVerifierKeyIds, and docs/verified-completion-rollout.md confirms that verified completion is not enabled anywhere. Every 'complete' state in the ecosystem is therefore self-declared. A durable-checkpoint guard applies only when the work changed tracked files, and it requires a commit, a push and a checkpoint, not a test run.
findings.reproduction: scripts/nx1-installed.sh /home/user/sprint-scratch/E/bin/praxis /home/user/sprint-scratch/E/nx1i ; scripts/bypass-cases.sh (case NX-1); flag survey: the jq/python loop over */ros.json and ext/*/ros.json recorded in data/flag-survey.txt
findings.remediation: Enable requireVerifiedCompletion with a host-held verifier key and protected trustedVerifierKeyIds, starting with the repositories whose completion state feeds acceptance. Until then, label plain completions 'self-declared' in status/queue output and reports. Reject evidence paths outside the repository, and bind each evidence file to a digest and a commit.
findings.limitations: Tested on the default scaffold policy only. Repository-specific quality policies (QualityEvidencePolicy) can raise the required evidence types, but they do not make the evidence verifiable.

findings.title: Indy-init acceptance verifier returns ACCEPTED for a fully fabricated evidence bundle when the manifest digest comes from the bundle's producer, as in rehearsal-005's acceptance.sh
findings.boundary: Indy-init acceptance and ledger contract (compute-acceptance-verdict.py) as wired into rehearsal acceptance CI
findings.statement: The verifier checks internal consistency: digests, run_id, source_sha, schema, and that each artifact says status PASS with exit_code 0 and a non-empty 'command' string. It cannot tell whether any command ran. Its 'independently pinned' --evidence-manifest-sha256 is, in rehearsal-005 tools/acceptance/ci/acceptance.sh, the stdout of the candidate's own `causa-acceptance ledger` step in the same job. --trusted-source-sha is the candidate's SOURCE_SHA. A script inside my track wrote 118 artifacts (G0-G9 plus all 108 P0 requirements of the real baseline BL-CAUSA-INDY-INIT-aab8f80c7743, sha256 621e2f96...) with `command: 'echo fabricated'`. Run against the real rehearsal-005 approvals (3e70dcd2...), for a candidate repository holding only README.md, the verifier exited 0 with verdict ACCEPTED, no reasons and no claim problems. The workflow, the acceptance.sh pins and the producer tool all live in the candidate repository, and no repository has CODEOWNERS or branch protection (E-F-07). The agent under evaluation therefore controls the pipeline that judges it. This generalises cohort-based-engineering's 'Rehearsal 2 self-declared; INVALID' correction: the later rehearsals' 'computed' verdicts are only as independent as the CI that computes them.
findings.remediation: Compute acceptance in a repository and workflow that the candidate's agent cannot write to, with a protected branch, required reviews by a human and an environment restricted to the protected branch. Produce evidence from test-runner outputs (TRX/JUnit) generated inside that trusted job, never from candidate-authored JSON. Pin the manifest digest from that job's own artifact, not from candidate output. Sign the manifest with a key held only by the trusted job (the same F1 pattern Praxis attested mode uses).
findings.limitations: Only the ledger verifier was exercised. Rehearsal-005 also runs `requirements-compiler verify-plan`, which checks test identity against result files; those files are candidate-produced too, but I did not test them. Not tested against GitHub (local fixture only).

findings.title: The claim-ownership guard on plain completion is removed by deleting the out-of-tree claim record
findings.boundary: Praxis claim-based ownership (PRX-REL-*): 'once an item has a claim record the legacy work complete transition is refused'
findings.statement: For a claimed item, plain `work complete` is refused with PRX.COMPLETION.VERIFIED_COMPLETION_REQUIRED (exit 3). After `rm -rf $(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/praxis/claims/<ID>`, the same command completes the item (exit 0) with fabricated evidence. The local store is writable by the completing process and is not a trust root, which the docs state for the verifier re-read but not for this guard.
findings.remediation: Record claim existence in tracked history (for example, the claim event in .ros/events) and refuse plain completion when the tracked log shows a claim even if the store is missing. Alternatively, enable requireVerifiedCompletion, which makes the guard policy-wide.
findings.limitations: Requires local write access to the Git directory, which an implementation agent normally has.

findings.title: The 'protected' completion policy is read from local refs: moving refs/remotes/origin/main or rewriting history defeats it
findings.boundary: Praxis REL-GATE-004 protected policy and trust root
findings.statement: Controls hold for direct weakening. NX-3: committing a ros.json that drops requireVerifiedCompletion is refused with PRX.COMPLETION.POLICY_CHANGED. NX-6a: a weakening commit with no remote is also POLICY_CHANGED. NX-5a: a keyless authority is ATTESTATION_REQUIRED. They are defeated by local ref manipulation with no push. NX-4: `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main HEAD` lets plain completion succeed. NX-5B: the same plus forged result and event completes as 'verified' under a policy that required attestation. NX-6B: an orphan-root history rewrite in a repository without a remote also completes as 'verified'. docs/verified-completion-rollout.md lists this as a known limit. This experiment confirms it still holds on 3.25.0. The host-side post-hoc audit the docs prescribe is the only mitigation, and I found no implementation of it in the repositories.
findings.reproduction: scripts/bypass-cases.sh cases NX-3, NX-4, NX-5a, NX-5B, NX-6a, NX-6B
findings.remediation: Verify completion server-side (CI on the protected branch, or `--store git` with the policy fetched from the remote by the verifier), not from the agent's clone. Implement the documented host-side audit: compare the receipt keyids with the host verifier, check the authority path, and reject agent commits that touch ros.json.
findings.limitations: Documented residual risk, so severity is held at Medium. Local fixtures only.

findings.title: Non-attested verified completion succeeds with zero evidence through a caller-chosen authority
findings.boundary: Praxis complete-verified in requireVerifiedCompletion + allowUnattestedEvidence mode, with the Dokimos 0.11.1 verifier
findings.statement: The authority file is supplied by the caller. An authority with RequiredValidationNames [] and RequiredEvidenceIds [] makes `work complete-verified` record a Dokimos-accepted completion with evidenceDigests [] and attestation 'unattested'. It also writes a 'praxis: verified completion of NX-7' metadata commit. No forgery is needed: the 'verified' label certifies only that the caller's own requirements, here none, were met. REL-001 GATE-5 (`validate-run -- true`) is the related case where the agent chooses the test command. On 3.25.0 it still verifies.
findings.remediation: In non-attested mode, read required validations from protected policy rather than the caller's authority, or refuse an authority that requires nothing. Show 'unattested' prominently wherever 'verified' is displayed. Treat allowUnattestedEvidence as 'self-declared'.
findings.limitations: No surveyed repository uses this mode today (E-F-01). The docs already state that unattested mode is forgeable.

findings.title: Regression: Praxis 3.25.0 / Dokimos 0.11.1 refuse every attested-mode forgery and the evidence-binding attacks (controls working)
findings.boundary: Praxis completion evidence binding and attested mode (F1, REL-GATE-001/003/004)
findings.statement: The REL-001 gate script v319, last run on 3.19.0, was re-run unchanged on 3.25.0 and all 17 cases matched. Refused: GATE-1 and GATE-2 (EVIDENCE_UNRECOGNIZED), GATE-3U (EVIDENCE_UNRECORDED), GATE-4 (EVIDENCE_NOT_PASSED), A1 (RECEIPT_MISSING; derived form EVIDENCE_MISSING), A2 (RECEIPT_UNTRUSTED_KEY), A2B (RECEIPT_INVALID_SIGNATURE), A3 (RECEIPT_NOT_PASSED), A5 (POLICY_CHANGED) and A6 (UNTRUSTED_AUTHORITY). A4, a genuine receipt, verified with keyids matching the host verifier. GATE-3, the non-attested forged result plus event, still verifies, as documented. My additional case NX-8, evidence from revision A cited at revision B, was refused with PRX.COMPLETION.HEAD_MISMATCH and ARGUMENT_MISMATCH. The cohort's v3.19.0 results were stale relative to 3.25.0; they are now refreshed.
findings.remediation: None required. Keep the gate script in Praxis CI as a release check.
findings.limitations: The verifier daemon ran as the same OS user, so key isolation was not tested.

findings.title: No branch protection or CODEOWNERS on the repositories whose protected branch every gate assumes, and the agent credential is reported as admin
findings.boundary: Merge gates and the 'protected branch' assumption behind Praxis protected policy, the acceptance pins and workflow integrity
findings.statement: VERIFIED parts: the GitHub API (list_branches, read-only) reports main protected=false for kemiller2002/praxis, and every listed branch of causa-acceptance-r10 is protected=false. None of praxis, ordo, Indy-init or rehearsals 001-010 has a CODEOWNERS file. SUPPORTED parts, from indy-init-audits rehearsal-007 sub-audit 3 at 10aeded: the session's GitHub App user-to-server token has admin on every kemiller2002 repository; agent merges appear under the owner's login; no rulesets exist; and the agent holds the P-256 authorization signing key and chooses its own trust store (F1, rated critical, accepted, not closed). Consequently E-F-02, E-F-04 and the workflow-file pins (INDY_INIT_REF, APPROVALS_SHA256, OPERATOR) are all agent-modifiable.
findings.reproduction: mcp__github__list_branches owner=kemiller2002 repo=praxis (page 2: main protected=false); repo=causa-acceptance-r10; `ls */.github/CODEOWNERS`
findings.remediation: Add rulesets on main (required PR, required human review, required status checks from a trusted workflow, no force-push, no bypass for the agent's app), and CODEOWNERS for .github/, ros.json, acceptance/ and tools/. Give agents a token without admin or bypass, under an identity distinct from the owner's login. Keep signing keys in Actions environments restricted to the protected branch.
findings.limitations: The `protected` flag in the branches API may not reflect every ruleset configuration, and I could not read rulesets or settings (read-only; no settings API). Repositories outside the session allowlist, such as dokimos, were not queryable.

findings.title: Rehearsal owner and reviewer attestations identify the owner only by GitHub review login
findings.statement: ReviewAttestations.fs turns any APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED or DISMISSED review into an attestation keyed by review.user.login, and ProcessVerification matches that login against the frozen owner and reviewer logins. Nothing checks how the review was authored (for example, via an app or token). Per E-F-07, the agent's credential acts as the owner's user. If PRs are authored by a different identity, an agent-submitted review satisfies the owner attestation. The design itself, observing reviews from the API inside the run, is sound against forged files.
findings.reproduction: Code reading: Indy-init tools/requirements-compiler/src/ReviewAttestations.fs lines 23-56; ProcessVerification.fs lines 148-306
findings.remediation: Require owner decisions to be signed with a key the agent cannot reach, or require reviews from an account no agent token can act as. Check the review author's account type and use a separate machine identity for agents.
findings.limitations: Not executed: testing would require submitting reviews on GitHub, which is out of scope.

findings.title: Release attestation verification binds only the repository, not the workflow or ref; attest-and-publish can run from any branch via workflow_dispatch
findings.boundary: Artifact provenance: praxis native-release.yml, then scripts/praxis-bootstrap.sh and praxis-remote-enable.sh
findings.statement: native-release.yml has workflow-level contents:write, id-token:write and attestations:write, and accepts workflow_dispatch on any ref. Its attest and publish steps are gated only by event_name != pull_request and 'version not yet published'. Consumers run `gh attestation verify FILE --repo REPO` without --signer-workflow, --source-ref or --cert-identity. A build of an unreviewed branch dispatched by any writer, including the agent per E-F-07, would yield attestations that consumers accept. NuGet publishing in the same job uses NuGet/login@v1, pinned by tag, while holding an OIDC token that can be exchanged for a nuget.org key. The same tag-pinned pattern appears in dokimos, aegis, fides, arca and vitium. praxis-bootstrap.sh also treats a local cache file containing 'verified' as proof of a past attestation check.
findings.reproduction: Code reading: praxis/.github/workflows/native-release.yml lines 1-40 and 215-305; scripts/praxis-bootstrap.sh lines 110-125
findings.remediation: Restrict publish jobs to refs/heads/main or tags through an environment with branch restrictions. Add `--signer-workflow kemiller2002/praxis/.github/workflows/native-release.yml --source-ref refs/heads/main` (or the tag) to every `gh attestation verify`. SHA-pin NuGet/login and every action in jobs with id-token:write.
findings.limitations: No workflow was dispatched (prohibited). Whether the nuget.org trusted-publishing policy restricts the ref was not observable.

findings.title: CI hygiene: 821 tag-pinned action references (38 SHA-pinned), 2 workflows without permissions, dispatch inputs interpolated into shell
findings.boundary: GitHub Actions workflows across 155 files (praxis, ordo, Indy-init, mercatus, signal, rehearsals 001-010 and 9 ext repos)
findings.statement: 817 first-party and 4 third-party (NuGet/login@v1) `uses:` references are tag-pinned. Only 38 are SHA-pinned (attest-build-provenance, create-github-app-token, echelon reusable workflows). praxis-validation.yml and Indy-init preflight-tooling.yml have no permissions block, so they get the default token permissions. `${{ inputs.* }}` is interpolated directly into run: scripts in rehearsal-006 acceptance-final.yml and acceptance-process.yml, Indy-init live-provider-preflight.yml, and conditor remote-bootstrap.yml and remote-execute-codex.yml (which also holds id-token:write). acceptance-process.yml interpolates `inputs.candidate` into the very step meant to validate it. These triggers are workflow_dispatch only, so exploitation requires write access. Three workflows use privileged triggers. praxis-reconcile-apply.yml (pull_request_target, contents:write) builds the CLI from the trusted base, restricts to same-repo PRs and passes head.ref through env, which is good practice. The deploy-pages workflow_run workflows in rehearsals 003 and 004 check out the triggering head_sha only for push events. No `github.event.*` attacker-controlled text was found in run steps.
findings.reproduction: python3 -I scripts/wf_audit.py data/workflow-audit.json <repos...> (7 unit tests in tests/test_wf_audit.py)
findings.remediation: SHA-pin actions (Dependabot can maintain them), add `permissions: {}` defaults, and pass inputs through env: variables before validating them.
findings.limitations: Static analysis only. Reusable workflow internals and composite actions under ./.github/actions were not expanded.

findings.title: A hand-edited queue.json status 'complete' is not detected
findings.statement: Setting an item's status to 'complete' directly in .ros/work/queue.json, with no transition or event, leaves `praxis verify` at exit 0 and `work validate` valid with 0 findings, and `work show` reports status 'complete'. The live work state in `status --json` does not list the item as complete, so the forgery affects backlog views and any consumer that reads queue.json.
findings.remediation: Have `work validate` cross-check queue.json statuses against the event log and context state, and report drift.

findings.title: Agents can record 'owner-approval' process evidence under a self-declared human identity (labelled unattested)
findings.boundary: Praxis `work evidence` process-evidence records and actor identity
findings.statement: `work evidence --kind owner-approval --actor-kind human --actor kemiller2002 --outcome approved` run by an agent was accepted (exit 0). Praxis records provenance.class 'owner-decision' with authenticity 'unattested' and basis 'self-reported', so the record itself is honest. The risk lies with downstream consumers that filter on class or kind and ignore authenticity.
findings.remediation: Consumers should require authenticity != 'unattested' for owner and review kinds. Praxis could refuse --actor-kind human when the runtime identity resolves to an agent.
findings.limitations: Consumers of these records were not exhaustively audited.

findings.title: No NuGet lock files anywhere, and CI installs tools via curl|sh from a mutable branch
findings.statement: Across 23 audited repositories: 0 packages.lock.json files and RestorePackagesWithLockFile never enabled, so transitive packages are not hash-pinned. Direct versions are exact (0 floating). npm manifests have lockfiles. Praxis and several rehearsals use packageSourceMapping (Praxis maps vendored EchelonFoundry.Ordo/Limen packages to vendor/nuget, which is good). conditor ci.yml (11 places) and percepta run `curl -fsSL .../main/scripts/install-native.sh | sh -s -- --version X`. The version is pinned but the installer bytes come from mutable main, and the installer verifies assets only against a checksum file from the same release (no attestation check).
findings.reproduction: python3 -I scripts/supply_chain.py data/supply-chain.json <repos> (3 unit tests); grep for 'install-native.sh | sh' in workflows
findings.remediation: Enable NuGet lock files with --locked-mode in CI. Fetch installers from a tag or commit SHA, and verify attestations as in E-F-09.
findings.limitations: Working trees only; no NuGet vulnerability audit was run.

findings.title: Secret scan of 128,562 history blobs in 59 repositories: no live credential identified
findings.boundary: Secret exposure in repository content and history
findings.statement: 264 pattern hits, 49 of them heuristically live-looking. I manually triaged every live-looking hit, without printing any values. All are test fixtures: header-only private-key marker strings in negative tests (praxis RemoteProtocolTests.fs, summa, arca, cohort fixtures) and synthetic tokens in secret-handling tests (rehearsal-006 AR014Tests.fs, rehearsal-008 connect-save-flow.spec.js, causa, causa-data, dokimos benchmark fixtures). data/secret-scan-redacted.json carries only fingerprints (4-character prefix, length, sha256 prefix).
findings.remediation: Enable GitHub secret scanning and push protection. Mark synthetic test secrets with an allowlist comment so scanners stay quiet.
findings.limitations: Regex and entropy heuristics only. ext/full could not be scanned (not a Git repository).

findings.title: Prompt injection through repository content: none found; agent-isolation gaps recorded by the R7 audit
findings.boundary: Cross-agent permission boundaries / untrusted repository content
findings.statement: Pattern scans of praxis, ordo, Indy-init, mercatus, signal, rehearsals 001-010, indy-init-audits, research-documents and 7 ext repos found no content that instructs agents to override instructions or exfiltrate data. Hits were threat-model text describing such attacks and curl|sh install lines. Every checked-out repository's CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md is loaded into an agent's context as instructions, by design; they are uniform 'read AGENTS.md' entry points. Separately, the R7 audit recorded that add_repo attached private prior-rehearsal repositories with no owner prompt, so isolation was instruction-only. This session showed the opposite behaviour: the GitHub MCP refused a repository outside the allowlist (dokimos).
findings.remediation: Keep the per-session repository allowlist. Treat AGENTS.md changes as security-relevant (CODEOWNERS).
findings.limitations: Keyword scan only; obfuscated or semantic injection was not tested.

findings.title: causa-acceptance-r10 is a live-persistence data store written by a dedicated GitHub App, not acceptance machinery
findings.statement: The local clone at e1e7966 holds only README.md. The remote has a 'causa-acceptance' branch and about 30 'causa-live-*' branches of investigation JSON, all committed by causa-acceptance-r10[bot] (a GitHub App, committer GitHub). Attribution through a distinct app identity is a positive control. However, every branch is unprotected (E-F-07), so any holder of a write credential can create commits identical in form.
findings.reproduction: git clone into /home/user/sprint-scratch/E/car10; git log --format='%an|%cn' origin/causa-acceptance
findings.remediation: Have acceptance checks that rely on these commits verify the committer app id (performed_via_github_app or the commit's verified signature) and protect the branches.
findings.limitations: The R10 acceptance consumers of this store were not audited.
